document: ET-8b — gen2 differs from gen1 at DECISION 3 ONLY. Recorded 15:38Z, before either seed's arm reported.
why_this_is_structural_and_not_a_bug: decision 1's state depends only on the TASK — nothing has happened yet — so every generation fits d1 on the same states and gets the same head.
decision 2's state depends on decision 1's pick. Since the d1 heads are identical, the d2 states are identical, so the d2 heads are identical.

decision 3's state depends on decision 2's pick. gen1's source trajectories were steered by GEN0's d2 head; gen2's by GEN1's d2 head, and those differ — so the d3 states differ and only the d3 head moves.
🔴_WHAT_IT_MEANS_FOR_THE_READING: gen2 vs gen1 isolates the DECISION-3 HEAD. Any difference the paired result shows is attributable to that one head and nothing else — which makes it a cleaner comparison than gen1 vs gen0 was, and also a much smaller surface on which to move.
🔵_AND_IT_BOUNDS_THE_SERIES: each generation can only change one decision further down the loop, and the loop has three. gen1 moved d2 and d3; gen2 moves d3; a gen3 would have nothing left to move at this budget. 理 11800 closed VIII-b's package after gen2 on other grounds; this is an independent structural reason the same line falls there.
⚠️_what_I_am_NOT_claiming: that gen0's and gen1's d1 heads are byte-identical. They are not, but their npz differ in FORMAT — gen0's predates the train_ranges field — so md5 cannot settle it and I did not compare the weights themselves.
